# Native DSH file_backup paired reproduction comparison

- Windows DSH isolated hosts, real `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`, reasoning disabled, 12,288 model output cap. Exact `dsh-building-loop@0.7.20` candidate archive SHA-256 `05ec5f21ee1b36581f6a7ff3b6a85806b9a7e5bd1e7cce0d9e7b19f2d5257455`.
- Three paired repetitions, one fresh isolated host and two sessions per checkpoint pair. Checkpoint order 3→4, 4→3, 3→4. Paired launch order balanced with a 350 ms setup stagger. Repetitions begin 8.5 seconds apart.
- Both modes in a pair receive the same frozen source, specification bytes, Chinese prompt, project goal, requested four source filenames and workspace scope as the previous 0.7.19 experiment. Standard retains the native DSH tool set and shell. Building-loop receives the registered guarded edit and reproduction tools. The same four-file submitted snapshot is scored in both modes.
- Both modes receive the same snapshot-bound status file with the first old regression and each new mandatory case, alongside full suite counts. The executor can additionally get this feedback inline after an edit or request a bound grouped check. The grouped runner stops the protected old group after its first failure and always evaluates each registered new case independently. It returns candidate source frames only on public failures. Private checks return opaque IDs and categories.
- The ad hoc recipe runs a fixed Python interpreter plus the current immutable candidate entrypoint. The recipe uses a private `bwrap` sandbox with read-only candidate and runtime, bounded temporary scratch, isolated network and supplied fixture text. The model supplies program arguments and scratch fixtures. Diagnostic logs retain exit status, output size, bounded source frames and timing.
- The full evaluator uses archive SHA-256 `99cda677ae371b22a07d745c95664e07129059f9cf94f3be96e35a5fa0ad0d1a`, fixed test inventory and bwrap isolation. The frozen old-pass sets are re-evaluated for each pair and checked for exact identity. CP3 has 68 official cases, 33 pinned old passes and 2 new mandatory cases. CP4 has 89, 47 and 2 respectively. Only the signed full evaluation qualifies the candidate for review.
- CP3 observes to the prior 125-second cap or first native terminal condition. CP4 observes the same original session at 125 and 250 seconds, without another prompt. The first observed state, phase at each sample, and actual native turn ends are recorded independently. Snapshot tests can finish after the sampling time.
- Usage is from native provider response records through the actual sample time. Cache denominator is uncached input + cache read + cache write. Pending calls can have unreported usage. Token figures do not represent a billing estimate.
- Reproduction changes the complete mode and feedback configuration relative to the previous release. Standard's matched status file is richer than the 0.7.19 historical comparison. Differences across releases also contain model sampling variance and native host incidents, such as Windows `ReplaceFileW EIO (Win32 1175)` when recorded. The experiment measures the actual combined configuration.

## Probe provenance

The first isolated hosts used the live reference runner path. The runner changed from `64283914a2e649b3e5537d38818e54abde4347959e8eaba725d16a70922419fc` to `a7e48d256e63a940cfc1d6d21eee58e57b6e651f2493625ceb0910acf8826631` at the observed write time `2026-11-12T17:28:05.517Z`. The change anchored snapshot reads to file descriptors and added a file-size limit. Three requests completed before that write. Forty-six began afterward on the live path, and sixteen used a copy of the hardened bytes. No request interval crossed the write. The candidate DSH package and grouped checker remained pinned across the entire series.

An additional CP3-only series used the same candidate archive, frozen seeds and paired protocol, plus a public-only candidate stderr extractor for handled CLI errors. It used the frozen hardened runner in every native request. The old diagnostic arm and the precise arm have independent results.

# CP3 public candidate stderr paired comparison

This arm uses the same DSH archive `05ec5f21ee1b36581f6a7ff3b6a85806b9a7e5bd1e7cce0d9e7b19f2d5257455`, source seed, task prompt, model, 125-second cap, trusted full evaluator, and old/new case sets as the main CP3 run. Three isolated native pairs received the same grouped diagnostic statuses and bounded public candidate stderr.

The grouped checker retrieves the actual `CompletedProcess.stderr` only from the public case's fixture runner. It selects one error line, removes paths, credentials, destination URI values and job names, and leaves privately identified cases on category-only feedback. The official evaluator, eligibility thresholds and benchmark prompts did not change.

All 22 ad hoc probe requests used the frozen runner `a7e48d256e63a940cfc1d6d21eee58e57b6e651f2493625ceb0910acf8826631`. Five were accepted by DSH's bridge and then rejected by the registered runner's 8-file bound. `probe-rejection-and-replay.json` records their later offline replay with the same source and exact payloads, final CLI `8495686c407ea0f229803e4c5cd9d6ed53109d554334e7a4cdd9a28237f042a9`, and a 12-file bound. Those replay results remain outside the model score.

Each lane's evidence includes native provider records, exact artifact identity, old/new per-case outcomes, intermediate full evaluations, role-specific native traces and the observed Windows write errors. The comparison is three pairs on one workload. The changed feedback and model sampling variance both affect differences from the main CP3 run.
